title: Triage-to-Rehabilitation Incident Lifecycle Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the end-to-end incident lifecycle used at Redwood Inference: triage -> containment -> stabilization -> rehabilitation -> postmortem. It prioritizes rapid customer impact reduction, clear ownership handoffs, and measurable verification of follow-up actions. Use this as the canonical runbook for production-facing serving incidents (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane).

Scope:
- Applies to production services supporting inference requests, embedding pipelines, and the control plane.
- Intended audience: first responders, SREs, product incident leads, Customer Success reps acting as customer liaisons.

Definitions:
- Severity levels: S1 (major outage, multi-region customer impact), S2 (single-region high-impact), S3 (degraded but non-critical).
- Triage: initial acknowledgement and impact assessment (first 0-10 minutes).
- Containment: actions to stop escalation of impact (10-45 minutes).
- Stabilization: hold state where customer-visible impact is removed and safe rollouts are prepared (45 minutes - 6 hours).
- Rehabilitation: engineering fixes, rollbacks, capacity restores, tests, and canary rollouts (6 hours - 14 days).
- Verification: completed validation of post-incident actions (up to 30 days depending on action).

Incident lifecycle (phase goals and timeboxes):
1) Triage (0-10 minutes)
   - Goals: acknowledge pager, determine severity, create incident channel, assign Incident Commander (IC).
   - Targets: pager ack <= 3 minutes; incident declared/dismissed <= 10 minutes.
   - Outputs: incident channel, initial impact statement, link to core dashboards.
2) Containment (10-45 minutes)
   - Goals: stop customer-facing degradation.
   - Typical actions: enable circuit-breakers, route to fallback models, disable noisy tenants, short-term scaling or region failover.
   - Targets: reduce error rate by >= 80% or bring latency within SLO within 45 minutes.
3) Stabilization (45 minutes - 6 hours)
   - Goals: stabilize metrics, lock mitigations, avoid repeated flips.
   - Outputs: pinned temporary config, adjusted alerts to avoid noisy pages, scheduled rehab plan.
4) Rehabilitation (6 hours - 14 days)
   - Goals: implement engineering fix, full capacity restore, regression test, and safe rollout.
   - Outputs: PRs, canary runs, monitoring dashboards with new detectors.
5) Postmortem & Prevention (publish within 7 days for S1/S2)
   - Goals: blameless root-cause analysis, SMART action items with owners and verification dates.

Roles and responsibilities:
- First Responder: acknowledges page, performs quick triage checks, posts initial notes in channel.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, decides containment strategy, owns executive comms drafts.
- SMEs: runtime, model-serving, infra, networking, observability.
- Customer Liaison: Customer Success/Account lead who owns external messaging and customer follow-up.
- SRE Lead: monitors elapsed time against escalation thresholds and triggers exec notifications if needed.

Core runbook checks (first 10 minutes):
- Health checks and high-level signals:
  1) Platform health: curl -s https://status.redwood-inference.internal/api/health | jq .
  2) Alert stream: check pager history and alerting dashboard
  3) Per-region error rates: /dashboards/serving/errors?window=5m
- Quick interrogations (commands):
  - kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide --selector=service=api | grep CrashLoopBackOff
  - redis-cli -h kv-cache INFO memory
  - rwictl deployments list --region us-west

Common mitigations (examples):
- Route traffic to fallback model (quantized/smaller):
  rwictl route set --model redwood-small-q8 --percent 100 --selector region=us-west
- Scale worker pool (temporary):
  terraform apply -var='worker_count=64' modules/serving/scale.tf
- Isolate tenant causing noisy behavior: update access control list or temporarily disable tenant key.
- Evict KV cache prefix if cache thrash is suspected: redis-cli -h kv-cache EVAL \"return redis.call('del', KEYS[1])\" 1 prefix:key

Containment decision matrix (text table):
Trigger | Immediate Action | Rationale
"Tail latency > 3x baseline for core endpoints" | Reduce max_seq_length to 512 for affected routes and enable prefix caching | Lowers average CPU/GPU work per request
"Pod OOMs on model decoder" | Cordon node, restart affected pods, failover to warm spare pool | Prevents repeating OOMs and isolates faulty node
"Error rate concentrated in single tenant" | Throttle or disable tenant traffic, open support ticket for tenant owner | Restores service for other customers quickly

Escalation thresholds:
- If mitigation fails to reduce impact within 30 minutes -> escalate to Eng SRE lead and Product on-call.
- If we have sustained customer impact > 3 hours -> notify Exec on-call and Customer Success Director.
- For S1 incidents, prepare an initial executive brief within 60 minutes.

On-call rotation patterns and handoffs:
- Default: primary-week / secondary-week pairing. Primary receives pages; secondary maintains situational awareness and performs escalations when requested.
- High-traffic windows (holidays, launches): use micro-shifts (12-hour shifts) with 30-minute overlap for handoff.
- Handoff checklist (must be posted in incident channel):
  1) Current impact summary (one-liner)
  2) Mitigations in place and who applied them
  3) Outstanding actions with owners and ETA
  4) Dashboards & links (latency, errors, pods, routing rules)
  5) Next scheduled check-in time and on-call contact handles

Game day exercises and validation:
- Cadence: quarterly SRE-led drills; annual cross-functional customer-impact simulation.
- Scenario templates: KV-cache thrash under synthetic load, model-quality regression after a release, autoscaler misconfiguration, multi-region routing failure.
- Exercise runbook:
  1) Announce scope and objectives 24 hours in advance to participating teams.
  2) Execute scenario with synthetic traffic and faults.
  3) Capture timeline and decisions in the incident channel (source of truth).
  4) Score outcomes: time-to-detect, time-to-recover, correctness of mitigations.
  5) Produce remediation actions and update runbooks within 2 weeks.

Postmortem (blameless) checklist:
- Collect artifacts: logs, traces, deployment events, alert history, canary reports.
- Build timeline: minute-level for first hour; 5-15 minute buckets thereafter.
- Identify root cause(s), contributing factors, detection gaps, and mitigation gaps.
- Define action items (owner, due date, verification criteria).
- Publish on Confluence and schedule verification review meeting.

Status page and customer communication templates:
- Short (status header):
  "Investigating elevated error rates for text-generation API in us-west — engineers are working on mitigations."
- Medium (status body/update):
  "We are investigating elevated error rates and latency on the text-generation endpoint in the US-West region. Mitigation in progress: traffic is being routed to a fallback quantized model while engineering investigates the root cause. Next update: 30 minutes."
- Long (post-incident summary):
  "Root cause: memory growth in the model decoder after a kernel patch caused OOMs on serving nodes. Fix: reverted kernel patch, deployed memory-accounting telemetry, and completed a canary rollout. Impact: 2028-02-14 02:12 UTC to 2028-02-14 04:47 UTC. Customers affected were contacted directly. Follow-ups: automated memory sampling and post-deploy smoke tests scheduled."

Customer liaison templates (for Account Managers):
- Initial contact (short):
  "We are investigating an issue affecting text-generation latency in your region. Mitigation applied to reduce impact. We will update you within 30 minutes. — Redwood Incident Team"
- Follow-up with remediation summary:
  "Action taken: routed traffic to a quantized fallback model reducing error rate by 92%; reverted a kernel change that correlated with increased memory usage. Long-term fix ETA: 10 business days. We will proactively coordinate billing adjustments if applicable."

Governance, runbook hygiene, and metrics:
- Ownership: every runbook must list an owner and a quarterly review date at the top of the page.
- Runbook retirement: if a runbook is not exercised in 12 months, it must be reviewed for relevance or archived.
- Action verification: owners must report action status in the Reliability Dashboard until marked verified.
- Key metrics to track post-incident: time-to-detect (TTD), time-to-contain (TTC), time-to-recover (TTR), number of mitigations applied, and number of customer-impacting requests.

Appendix: copy/paste channel snippets
- INCIDENT header (copy into channel):
  "INCIDENT: [One-line summary] | IC: @username | Severity: S1/S2 | Impact: [customers/percent] | Mitigation: [short description]"
- HANDOFF snippet (at time of handoff):
  "HANDOFF: Summary: [one-liner]; Mitigations: [list]; Outstanding: [actions with owners]; Next check: [time]; Owner: @username"

Document metadata guidance (for page header):
- Recommended labels: incident-lifecycle, runbook, oncall, game-day, status-page
- Suggested reviewers: Daniel Kim, Priya Shah, Alex Nguyen

End of playbook. For questions or to propose edits, ping @maya.patel or open an edit request on the page.
